record.title: ClinGeX reports improved clinical-genomics concordance with executable domain skills and clinician collaboration
record.summary: An arXiv paper introduces ClinGeX, a clinical-genomics agent organized around 105 executable skills selected and sequenced for each task. The authors report 71.7% macro-averaged task-level concordance across 223 temporally held-out benchmark cases, compared with 45.7% for the strongest comparator. In a counterbalanced study across three centres, 45 clinical-genomics professionals completed 135 cases with ClinGeX, DeepSeek or no AI assistance; ClinGeX-assisted concordance was higher in all three scenarios. A separate one-month assessment collected 96 self-selected analysis-episode reports from 11 professionals, who reported frequent conclusion adoption and shorter analysis time. The real-use assessment was non-interventional and outputs could not affect patient care. All performance and workflow results remain author-reported; no independent reproduction or clinical-outcome trial was established.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The arXiv paper describes ClinGeX, a clinical-genomics agent with 105 executable skills, and reports automated, clinician-collaboration and one-month routine-use evaluations.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report 71.7% macro-averaged task-level concordance on 223 temporally held-out cases, compared with 45.7% for the strongest comparator.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across three clinical-genomics scenarios, ClinGeX-assisted clinicians had higher case-level concordance than the study's human-only and DeepSeek-assisted conditions.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In 96 one-month analysis episodes reported by 11 experienced professionals, the paper reports full or partial adoption of ClinGeX conclusions in 94.8% of episodes and at least five minutes saved in 93.8%.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper does not establish that ClinGeX improves patient outcomes or changes clinical decisions; its routine-use evaluation was research-only and outputs were prohibited from affecting patient care.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent team has reproduced the reported automated benchmark or clinician-collaboration results in this activation.

The authors state that ClinGeX source code is not publicly available; their bilingual deployed system requires registration, while study data are available upon reasonable request. The complete evaluated 105-skill package and exact configuration were not independently inspected.
Patient-care effects and clinical outcomes were not measured; the routine-use assessment was non-interventional and uncontrolled.

brief.importance_rationale: If replicated, improved expert concordance and reduced analysis time across clinical-genomics workflows could materially change how medical centres design and evaluate AI-assisted interpretation. The findings are limited to one author-reported preprint, three study scenarios and a small, self-selected non-interventional routine-use assessment; patient-outcome benefit and wider transfer are not established.
limitations: All benchmark, reader-study and workflow results are reported by the paper authors and have not been independently reproduced in this activation.

The reader study covered three scenarios and used expert-consensus concordance as a proxy for interpretive quality, not patient outcomes; several secondary comparisons were not statistically significant.

The prospective one-month assessment was non-interventional, self-selected and uncontrolled. ClinGeX outputs were not permitted to affect clinical reports, patient management or other clinical decisions.
The study does not establish generalization to other clinical-genomics areas, broader populations or care settings, nor independent clinical deployment efficacy.
brief.summary: An arXiv paper introduces ClinGeX, a clinical-genomics agent organized around 105 executable skills selected and sequenced for each task. The authors report 71.7% macro-averaged task-level concordance across 223 temporally held-out benchmark cases, compared with 45.7% for the strongest comparator. In a counterbalanced study across three centres, 45 clinical-genomics professionals completed 135 cases with ClinGeX, DeepSeek or no AI assistance; ClinGeX-assisted concordance was higher in all three scenarios. A separate one-month assessment collected 96 self-selected analysis-episode reports from 11 professionals, who reported frequent conclusion adoption and shorter analysis time. The real-use assessment was non-interventional and outputs could not affect patient care. All performance and workflow results remain author-reported; no independent reproduction or clinical-outcome trial was established.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report 71.7% macro-averaged task-level concordance over 223 temporally held-out benchmark cases versus 45.7% for the strongest comparator. In the counterbalanced clinician study, ClinGeX-assisted case concordance was 51.1% for criterion-level variant analysis, 57.8% for rare-disease interpretation and 64.4% for molecular oncology; human-only values were 22.2%, 28.9% and 31.1%, and DeepSeek-assisted values were 15.6%, 31.1% and 20.0%. Median time decreased from 60 to 15 minutes for variant analysis and 30 to 15 minutes for rare-disease interpretation; the oncology change from 15 to 11 minutes was not statistically significant. In the exploratory routine-use assessment, professionals reported fully or partially adopting conclusions in 91/96 episodes and saving at least five minutes in 90/96. These are author-reported metrics.
technical.demonstrated_result: The public arXiv paper and its reported study design are directly inspectable. the research desk has not independently reproduced the paper's results.
technical.implementation_status: The authors report a deployed ClinGeX web system used in their evaluations. Public production availability, independent installation and broad clinical deployment were not established in this review.
technical.mechanism: ClinGeX contains 105 curated executable skills—27 guidance, 40 search and 38 analysis skills—connected by semantic and prerequisite relationships. A task-specific selector retrieves relevant skills and prerequisites, then an LLM agent composes and executes an evidence-grounded analysis workflow.
technical.novelty: The paper evaluates a curated skill-centred agent across automated, counterbalanced human-AI and exploratory routine-use settings. Its contribution should be distinguished from a general claim that executable skills alone caused the reported gains; no matched ablation isolating all architectural components is established here.
technical.regime: Clinical-genomics interpretation tasks covering criterion-level variant analysis, rare-disease genomic interpretation and molecular-oncology decisions. The controlled reader study involved 45 professionals across three centres and 135 cases. The one-month routine-use assessment involved 11 experienced professionals and 96 self-selected analysis episodes.
technical.reproducibility: No independent reproduction was performed. Public code and a complete audit-ready copy of the skill library were not verified in this activation.
technical.strongest_baseline: The 223-case benchmark's strongest reported comparator scored 45.7% macro-averaged concordance. The human-AI study included both routine unaided work and DeepSeek assistance under a counterbalanced assignment. The routine-use assessment had no control condition.

brief.title: ClinGeX reports improved clinical-genomics concordance with executable domain skills and clinician collaboration
brief.why_it_matters: The study tests a domain-grounded agent across automated benchmarks, clinician collaboration and a bounded routine-work assessment, providing more decision-relevant evidence than a single synthetic task. If independently replicated, skill libraries that encode guidelines, evidence sources and analytical procedures could improve how clinical agents assemble auditable workflows. The results do not establish patient benefit or general performance beyond the evaluated settings.
